final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package with 75% RVC, unified labor enforcement (Article 4.3: identical 5% penalty floor, audit-triggered with 30-day cure, staggered audit schedules), 24-month compliance phase-in for integrated supply chains, six-year renewable sunset, Chapter 19 retained, and Canadian dairy protected. Canada's Cabinet brief is imminent; signature expected tomorrow morning if annex stability language satisfies auto/supply-chain concerns about mid-stream rule changes.
minority_objections: U.S. dairy sector demanded post-signature bilateral market-access negotiation, rejected by room as undermining Canada's protected dairy redline
Supply-chain manufacturers and auto industry raised unresolved concern about whether 12-month review could reinterpret RVC rules mid-phase-in
key_conflicts: Canada's initial rejection of 75% RVC as 'restructuring mandate' vs. USTR's non-negotiable floor
Multi-round dispute over whether labor enforcement was symmetric (one standard) or two-tier (different penalty triggers during Canada's phase-in)
Auto/supply-chain demand for RVC phase-in window vs. USTR's day-one 75% threshold, resolved via 24-month compliance milestones with audit-triggered penalties
key_concessions: Canada accepted 75% RVC with no sector carve-outs in exchange for 18-month labor audit phase-in and 24-month RVC compliance window
USTR granted Canada phased labor implementation (18 months) and RVC compliance milestones (24 months) while holding penalty floor identical across all three countries
U.S. accepted six-year renewable sunset (vs. hard sunset) and retention of Chapter 19 dispute settlement
red_lines: USTR: 75% RVC non-negotiable, no sector carve-outs
Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement must remain, dairy supply management protected, sunset must require trilateral consent to expire
Congress/Labor: labor enforcement must be symmetric (identical penalty floor) or ratification fails
Auto/supply-chain: no mid-stream rule reinterpretation during phase-in or investment commitments collapse
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Dairy sector's demand for scheduled market-access negotiation dismissed without exploring whether it could unlock broader agricultural support for ratification
Unresolved question of whether 12-month review allows USTR to tighten RVC interpretation—auto and supply-chain flagged this as deal-killer but received no written stability clause by transcript end

Labor union's concern about enforcement gaps in Mexico (whether penalties trigger on systematic wage violations or require worker complaints first) acknowledged but not resolved in Article 4.3 language
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional ratification hinges on members seeing full annex text confirming audit-triggered penalties and no mid-stream rule changes
Auto/supply-chain investment commitments depend on written stability clause preventing RVC reinterpretation at 12-month review
Canadian Cabinet approval depends on annex language showing penalty triggers only after audit detection, not day-one automatic penalties
U.S. dairy sector opposition could mobilize against ratification if no market-access pathway emerges post-signature
uncertainty_notes: Canada's Cabinet brief is in progress; signature expected tomorrow morning but contingent on annex language satisfying auto/supply-chain demand for stability clause against mid-stream rule changes. Congressional ratification risk remains elevated (73→76 by R8) due to members not yet seeing full treaty text. Labor enforcement symmetry resolved in principle (Article 4.3) but execution gaps remain on whether Mexican wage violations trigger penalties automatically or require worker complaints.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC was Canada's opening 'non-starter' (R1), drove multi-round conflict over sector carve-outs, and forced the 24-month compliance phase-in compromise (R7-R8) that unlocked Canada's signature path—decisive in shaping the package.
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Congress stated 'make-or-break piece for ratification' (R1), drove 4+ rounds demanding Article 4.3 text proving symmetric penalty floor, and USTR's clarification of audit-triggered penalties (R8) was explicitly framed as closing the ratification gap.
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Raised by dairy_ag (R1, R2) and Canada confirmed as Cabinet redline (R6), but USTR locked 'dairy stays protected' (R3) without concessions—acknowledged as politically sensitive but did not alter the trilateral terms.
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 as Cabinet mandate (R6), Mexico confirmed it stays in text (R6), but no negotiation occurred—it was preserved as-is rather than driving a concession or proposal.
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply-chain stated 'deal-killer' if hard sunset (R2), drove USTR to lock 'six-year renewable by mutual consent' in text (R3), and Canada demanded trilateral veto on expiration (R4)—directly shaped the sunset clause outcome.
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress warned 'members won't vote' without enforcement teeth (R1), demanded full annex text or 'kill this on ratification' (R7), and USTR's R8 clarification was explicitly to prevent ratification collapse—shaped multiple concessions and disclosure decisions.
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply-chain demanded compliance cost/sourcing certainty (R1), drove 24-month phase-in window (R7), and flagged mid-stream rule-change risk as '$50M+ tooling' deal-breaker (R8)—materially shaped the RVC implementation structure.
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR's R1 ultimatum 'Mexico accepted 75%, you match or we go bilateral' and Mexico's R2 'let's stop circling, sign trilateral' created explicit leverage—Canada's R3 acceptance of labor/RVC terms was direct response to this pressure.
